key_insight: The paper introduces a generalizable, systematic method for designing and evaluating LLM prompts that produce personalized, pedagogically aligned outputs — demonstrated by comparing six prompt templates for generating follow-up questions in a structured dialogue activity.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of evidence-based, repeatable methods for creating and assessing prompts in educational settings, where ensuring personalization and instructional alignment is critical.
method: Design six prompt templates that embed pedagogical and personalization considerations for follow-up question generation.
Apply a systematic evaluation framework combining quantitative metrics and qualitative human judgments to assess output quality, alignment, and personalization.
Compare template performance in a structured dialogue task to identify strengths, trade-offs, and best practices for prompt design.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners and EdTech developers a replicable toolkit to iterate on prompts and measure educational effectiveness, reducing the risk of generic or misaligned instructional outputs.
visual_elements: Flowchart of the evaluation pipeline (prompt design → LLM outputs → metrics & human review → template comparison)
Bar or radar chart comparing the six templates across key metrics (alignment, personalization, clarity, pedagogical value)
Annotated sample dialogue showing original student turn and alternative LLM-generated follow-up questions for each template
Scorecard/rubric iconography illustrating combined quantitative + qualitative scoring (teacher-in-the-loop)
paper_title: LLM Prompt Evaluation for Educational Applications
paper_authors: Langdon Holmes, Adam Coscia, Scott Crossley, Joon Suh Choi, Wesley Morris
